title: House of the Dragon Returns June 21. For Diaspora Fans, the Real Date Is June 22.
excerpt: Season 3 opens on the Battle of the Gullet, the bloodiest spectacle the franchise has ever attempted. Here's exactly when and where to watch it from the US, UK, Canada — and India.
body:
It has been almost two years since Westeros left us hanging. Two seasons of slow-burn dynastic poison, of Emma D'Arcy's Rhaenyra hardening from heir to war queen, of Matt Smith's Daemon staring into a weirwood tree and seeing things no Targaryen was meant to see. And now, after a wait that felt engineered to test our loyalty, **House of the Dragon** is back — Sunday, June 21, on HBO and HBO Max.

<youtube>https://youtube.com/watch?v=0JlMjgqduVw</youtube>

If you're reading this from Mumbai or Bengaluru, mark a different square on the calendar. For Indian viewers, Season 3 lands June 22 on **JioHotstar**, dropping a day after the global debut so you can wake up to dragonfire instead of staying up for it.

The season opens, by every account, on the **Battle of the Gullet** — a naval bloodbath that is being described as the single biggest battle the entire *Game of Thrones* universe has ever put on screen. If you read Fire & Blood, you know what's coming: ships splintering, dragons falling out of the sky into the sea, a body count that reshapes the war in a single night. The premiere episode runs a hefty 72 minutes, and HBO is clearly front-loading the spectacle. This is not a show easing back in. It's kicking the table over.

> "We're the only three people in the world who have come from our positions and ended up where we are. The Targaryens have been raised to speak High Valyrian and ride dragons. We haven't." — Tom Bennett, on the dragonseeds

That quote points to the season's most intriguing new thread. The **dragonseeds** — lowborn Targaryen bastards who can suddenly claim dragons of their own — are about to upend the rules of who gets to hold power in this world. It's a deliciously democratic wrinkle in a story otherwise obsessed with bloodlines, and the show seems to know it.

The core ensemble all return: **Emma D'Arcy** as Rhaenyra, **Matt Smith** as Daemon, **Olivia Cooke** as the perpetually grieving Alicent Hightower, **Ewan Mitchell** as the eyepatched menace Aemond, and **Tom Glynn-Carney** as the increasingly unhinged Aegon II. New faces join the carnage too — **James Norton** as Ormund Hightower, plus Tommy Flanagan and Dan Fogler stepping into the realm.

Smith, who remains the show's most magnetic presence, has teased that Daemon comes back changed. After those visions at Harrenhal — the three-eyed raven, Daenerys and her dragons, Rhaenyra on the Iron Throne — his rogue prince has found something close to faith. "There's this ethereal thing that's born into his soul," Smith said, "and suddenly there's a religious vigor in him." A Daemon with a sense of purpose is arguably more dangerous than a Daemon with none.

Eight episodes will roll out weekly through August 9, the same patient Sunday-night cadence that turned this prequel into appointment television. Season 2 averaged a staggering 25 million viewers an episode. Season 3 is positioned to do more, and it arrives with a notable first: concurrent ASL episodes, making this the most accessible season the franchise has produced.

**Where to watch, by geography:** In the US, you need HBO Max — $10.99/month with ads, $18.49 without. In the UK, it streams on Sky and NOW. In Canada, it's on Crave. And across India, JioHotstar carries it from June 22, the cheapest entry point of the lot for the diaspora's relatives back home. For NRIs juggling a US HBO Max login and a family WhatsApp group that's already three episodes deep on JioHotstar, the one-day gap is going to make for some very tense spoiler etiquette.

Here's the thing about this franchise: it has never been better than when it commits fully to its own cruelty. Season 1 was setup. Season 2 was the slow tightening of the noose. Season 3 is the war itself — dragons against dragons, kin against kin, the Dance of the Dragons finally living up to its name. If the Battle of the Gullet delivers what the books promise, the opening hour alone will be worth the two-year wait.

Set your reminders. Westeros is about to burn, and this time there's nowhere left to hide.
